_doc: Slice #180 — the calibration bands for the LIVE engine (tests/MarketEconomy.calibration.test.ts), as distinct from the pure-SalesProcess bands in data/sales-process.json (#94). Two band sets on purpose. `reference` is the DESIGN COMMITMENT — what a competent operation should realize once the economy is calibrated; it is the #94 band set, because a 0.75/0.75 operator should not close worse just because the rest of the game showed up. `live` is the MEASURED state of the game today: the test asserts `live` as a regression guard and reports the gap to `reference`, so the harness is green and honest rather than green and lying. Closing that gap is #286 (Pricing/Demand spine S14 calibration pass) — when it lands, `live` moves toward `reference` and this doc says so.

reference._doc: The #94 design commitment. Not asserted yet — see `live`.

live._doc: Measured at seed 20260806 pre-#286 over 601 worked ups in 369 days: 2.2% positive, 97.7% apathetic, 0.2% negative-deal, 96.8% warm walks, 51.0% of all arrivals lost to no_fit, 57.1% trade-acquisition rate. The gap to `reference` is not noise and not a harness artifact: the #94 harness demos every customer a PERFECT SPACED match (Value meter ~0.85), while a real tier-1 six-space lot yields the best-of-six (Value ~0.4). Reservation price is market x (reservationBase + Value*valueLift - sensitivity*sensitivityDrag), so the lower Value — combined with a price sensitivity of 1 - wealth/120000 that sits at 0.6-0.85 for most archetypes — drags willingness-to-pay under vehicleCost + minGross on most worked ups. They then walk as `no_close` off the below-floor branch (415 of them, against 37 patience-drain and 17 trust-collapse: the quadrant close is NOT what is rejecting these deals, the price floor is). Bands sit around the measured values with enough room that an unrelated tweak doesn't trip them and a real regression does.

earlyGame._doc: Slice #181 — the early-game FLOOR (tests/MarketEconomy.earlyGameFloor.test.ts). The same live engine `live` measures, run with the green solo operator the career starts you as (0.35/0.40 raw composites) instead of the competent 0.75/0.75: cold start, day 1, no comp history, one salesperson, NO used-car manager, no paid pre-buy inspections, default trade policy. It exists so the progression has a proven bottom — a career whose day-1 state performs like its end state has no progression in it. Measured at seed 20260806 over 200 worked ups in 110 days: 0.0% positive, 97.0% apathetic, 3.0% negative-but-deal (6 closes, EVERY ONE of them a low-trust forced close), 43.3% warm walks, 46.5% no_fit, 9 acquisitions / 8 completed recons, mean recon overrun 1.087x, $18.63/unit/day carrying. The shape of the floor is the finding: a green operator closes about as often as a competent one but cannot make ANY of those customers happy, and `trust_collapse` becomes the dominant walk reason (115 against #180's 17). The margins are distances from `live`/`reference` rather than a second pair of bands, so when #286 raises `live` the floor must move with it or the assertion fails.
earlyGame._reconDoc: The tail RATE is a ceiling guard, not a tight measurement: acquisitions are gated by sales, so a green six-space lot turns ~9 units in the whole window (13 even if ground out to 400 days) and 0 surprises fired against an expectation of ~0.45. A band that pretended to precision there would be banding luck. `reconOverrun` is the one with power — every completed recon contributes, and data/recon-variance.json's bucket mix implies a population mean of ~1.061 against the 1.087 measured. Both tighten on their own once #286 makes the lot turn. reconOverrunMin sits just under 1 on purpose: it asserts recon does not on average come in UNDER its estimate, which is what makes buying blind a cost rather than a coin flip.
